messages:
jamie: Heads-up — LumaPay signed for a private VPC deployment. They expect a ~3x traffic spike for their holiday promo (Nov 15–Dec 05). Need a quick sizing estimate: GPU hours, minimum runway, and procurement lead time. Baseline they gave: 100 qps steady, avg 120 tokens/req, p99 target <150ms. Who can run numbers and call out risks?
anya: I can run a back-of-the-envelope now. Do we know which model they want pinned? That changes throughput a lot.
mohit: Also which region? Cross-region private peering has bandwidth caps and adds ~10–20ms depending on colo. Could affect p99.
jamie: They want a 13B family model (customer ok with quantized variant). Region: us-east-1 colocated.
anya: OK — rough calc below. Assumptions: 3x peak factor, 24h sustained peak (worst-case planning), use quantized 13B at ~8k tokens/s per A100-like GPU (conservative).

```
# assumptions
baseline_qps = 100
peak_factor = 3
peak_qps = baseline_qps * peak_factor  # 300 rps
avg_tokens_per_req = 120
tokens_per_sec = peak_qps * avg_tokens_per_req  # 36,000 tps
per_gpu_tokens_sec = 8000
gpus_required = ceil(tokens_per_sec / per_gpu_tokens_sec)  # 5 GPUs
gpu_hours_per_day = gpus_required * 24  # 120 GPU-hours/day
planning_runway_days = 30  # recommend 30d buffer
monthly_gpu_hours = gpu_hours_per_day * 30 = 3600 GPU-hours
```

anya: So initial recommendation: 5 GPUs to meet sustained peak. For a 30-day runway plan for capacity/procurement we budget ~3600 GPU-hours. If we want p99 <150ms, we should target a 1.2x headroom for scheduling spikes => bump to 6 GPUs (144 GPU-hours/day).

lina: Can we reduce tokens/req? Caching common prefixes or using a short-context reranker would cut cost a lot. If we drop avg tokens to 80, tokens/sec becomes 24k => 3 GPUs. Worth proposing an optimization bundle to the customer. :bulb:
mohit: Network notes: private VPC in us-east-1 is fine but confirm they want cross-connect vs VPN. Cross-connect gives lower and consistent latency. Also watch NAT gateway egress for telemetry — could be a cost leak if telemetry is chatty.
procurement-bot: FYI procurement lead times for dedicated A100 instances (if customer wants on-prem pods procured via our channel) are ~6–8 weeks for new orders; if they reuse existing racks it's ~2–3 weeks for provisioning and testing.
ops-bot: Suggested autoscale policy: min=3, desired=5, max=8 with cooldown 90s and CPU/GPU-util triggers. Also enable prefix caching for the top-50 prompts LumaPay will send.
anya: Quick cost sketch using our internal unit cost (hosted-equivalent): suppose $X per GPU-hour (we'll fill in figure in proposal). At 6 GPUs (buffered) => 144 GPU-hours/day => ~4320 GPU-hours/month. If we can push optimizations (token reduction + caching) we can move to ~2000–2500 GPU-hours/month.
jamie: Good. Action items: 1) Anya: produce a 1-page sizing note with two scenarios (baseline conservative 6-GPU buffer, optimized 3-GPU config) and include cost estimates. 2) Mohit: confirm network peering options and egress estimate for telemetry. 3) Procurement-bot: confirm vendor lead times and quick-provision path. 4) Lina: sketch a prompt-caching plan and expected token reduction.
anya: I'll drop the note by EOD today. Will include a small table and the math.
mohit: I'll ping infra-sales for cross-connect options and get an estimate on per-GB egress + monitoring overhead.
procurement-bot: Noted — will validate lead-time and spare inventory; if they commit to a 6-month contract we can prioritize ordering (can shave ~2 weeks).
lina: I'll prototype a prefix cache metric to show hit-rate impact — should have numbers in 48h.
jamie: Perfect. Also flagging we should recommend an incremental rollout (canary week) to validate p99 without full capacity. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Saved action items to the deployment checklist and created ticket INFR-8721 for procurement + peering.
anya: One more callout — if LumaPay expects lots of short bursts (flash traffic), we might prefer more GPUs but lower batching sizes to keep p99; that's an ops tradeoff we'll document.
jamie: Thanks all. We'll sync tomorrow after the sizing note.
